learningObjective: Precisely characterize the defining property of SSA (Static Single Assignment) form and distinguish it from related notions.
stem: Which statement correctly defines Static Single Assignment (SSA) form?

options.text: Each variable is stored in a distinct memory location; SSA is a memory-layout property enforced by the register allocator.
Every variable is written exactly once at runtime along every execution path; loops therefore cannot be represented in SSA without unrolling.

Every variable in the intermediate representation is textually assigned in exactly one program statement, and phi (φ) functions are inserted at control-flow join points to merge different reaching definitions from predecessor blocks.
SSA requires all variables to be constants, since 'single assignment' means a value is fixed at compile time.

explanation: SSA is a syntactic property of the IR: each name has exactly one textual definition; φ-functions reconcile values that reach a join from different predecessors. Loops are representable in SSA — the loop-header uses a φ-function to merge the initial value with the value flowing back from the backedge. SSA is not about runtime write counts, storage locations, or compile-time constancy.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: SSA is an IR-level concept independent of memory allocation; register allocation happens later (often after out-of-SSA).
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: SSA is a syntactic (textual) property, not a runtime-execution constraint; loops are naturally expressed.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: standard SSA definition (textual single assignment + φ at joins).
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: SSA variables can take runtime values; single assignment means single textual definition, not compile-time constancy.

assumptions: Standard SSA as defined in Cytron et al. and canonical compiler textbooks.
nonImplications: Does not imply that φ-functions have a runtime cost; they are pseudo-instructions eliminated by out-of-SSA copy insertion.
Does not imply SSA is only useful for optimization; it also simplifies dataflow analysis reasoning.

distractorRationales.B: Confuses syntactic single-assignment with runtime execution behavior.
distractorRationales.D: Confuses single assignment with compile-time constant.

sourceRefs.locator: Ch. on SSA (§9 in EAC3): definition and construction
